stage1.impression: A sharp, instantly legible pun: the Earth wearing the Death Star's dish. The dish geometry is genuinely good. The ellipse is foreshortened along the radius and the inner rings sink toward the globe's centre, so it reads as a concave divot. The disc holds on paper and on ink. The one-colour cuts are the best drawings on the sheets, with the dish as a stark ring and dot, and the land-free cut for small sizes is sensible. Against it, the colour lead is an emoji-style globe with a warm bullseye on it. That is five hues, six with the violet variants, and the red, orange and yellow rings read as a hotspot or a target before anything else. The coasts are too fussy to draw from memory. The dish is jammed against the right edge with only a hairline of land beyond it. The one-colour 32 and 16 px versions turn to speckle. The violet cap makes the dish a pupil, and the violet trench reads as a sash cutting the globe in half. The motion is a generic sonar ping: a thin red ellipse leaves the dish rim and grows past the globe's outline as a flat ring on the paper. It fades through a long ghost tail (0.40-0.55 s), then holds still for about 0.45 s, and repeats identically every second. The figure itself never visibly moves (frame 02's dish matches frame 01's), so this animation could belong to any map pin.

keep: The dish's geometry: foreshortened along the radius, with the cone and dust cap sinking toward the globe's centre (depth 0.42). It reads as a real concave divot, the Death Star's signature, and as a driver (surround, cone, cap) in three flat colours. Keep this construction exactly.

The one-colour knock-out system: the disc and cone are solid, and the land, surround and cap are knocked out. The black-only and white-only figures are the strongest drawings on the sheets, and the land-free cut is the right answer at 24 px and under.

changes.problem: The dish is jammed against the right edge of the globe, so almost no earth shows outside it. That is the opposite of the owner's 'more earth on the outside'.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, 'colour' 300 px: the dish's far rim reaches 0.83 of the radius, leaving about 25 px of globe at the narrowest. The land there is a hairline crescent of Europe and West Africa. A 24-degree dish is 48 degrees of arc across, about as wide as the North Atlantic between Newfoundland and Iberia, so its clearance trims Newfoundland, Iberia, Morocco and Senegal. Sheet 2, 'black only' 64 px: that crescent and the white surround fuse into extra arcs. Sheet 1 #1: the red rim nearly touches the edge.
changes.expected: The dish moves about 0.07 of the radius in and slightly up, and keeps its 24-degree size. The band between its rim and the globe's edge widens from about 0.17 to 0.21 of the radius, about 31 px at 300 px. Europe and West Africa read as a real crescent of land to the right of the dish. The dish stays in the upper right, with its inner edge just clear of the centre.

accept.check: The narrowest band of ocean and land between the dish's red rim and the globe's edge is between 30 and 45 px wide (it is about 25 px now).

changes.problem: The ring of sound is a generic radar ping. It is a thin red outline that escapes the globe and spends most of its life as a flat ellipse on the paper, which is a stroke in a no-stroke system. Over the globe it nearly disappears.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frames 02-05 (0.13-0.53 s): by frame 03 (0.27 s) most of the ring lies outside the globe's outline on the paper, crossing the edge at two points. Over the globe, in luminance, the red is 1.4:1 against the ocean and 1.0:1 against the land. The trace is a soft hump peaking at 0.20 s (0.53 %), with nothing at the beat itself.
changes.expected: The ring becomes a knock-out in the ground colour, so it shows only where it crosses the globe. On paper it is a light band sweeping out from the dish over the Atlantic and the Americas and vanishing at the edge; on ink it is a dark band. Nothing is drawn on the ground. Because the ring leaves the red rim in a contrasting colour, each beat gets a sharp start: the trace peaks at about 0.07 s instead of 0.20 s.

accept.check: The ring is visible only where it crosses the globe, and no part of it is drawn on the ground outside the globe.

changes.problem: The kick is invisible. The push lasts 0.06 s and is undone by 0.15 s, so the pushed pose exists for one frame and no storyboard frame shows it.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frames 01 and 02 (0.00 s and 0.13 s): the dish looks identical. The trace at 0.00-0.03 s reads 0.06 % (sidecar 0.00058), under the 0.2 % stillness line, so the kick does not even count as motion.
changes.parameter: CORE push timing: a hold phase
changes.description: Keep the push as it is (0 to 0.06 s, cubic ease-out). Then hold the pushed driver still for 0.07 s, to 0.13 s. Return through the overshoot (depth 0.50) at 0.24 s instead of 0.15 s, and come to rest by 0.42 s instead of 0.30 s. The beat stays at 1.0 s.
changes.expected: The pushed pose stays on screen for about three frames (0.03-0.13 s), and storyboard frame 02 catches it. The driver then sinks back past rest and settles while the ring crosses the globe. The figure is still from about 0.45 s until the next beat.

accept.check: The driver is still pushed out: the yellow dust cap sits visibly nearer the dish's centre than in frame 01.

changes.problem: The push stops at depth 0.12, so the rings stay off centre and the divot never visibly fills. The speaker's defining move does not read.
changes.evidence: Card: going from depth 0.42 to 0.12 moves the dust cap only about 0.05 of the radius, 3-4 px at storyboard scale. Sheet 3 trace at 0.00-0.03 s: 0.06 %. No frame on sheet 3 shows the rings re-centred.
changes.parameter: CORE push: depth target (DISH.depth at full push)
changes.expected: On the beat the divot pops flush: the cone and cap snap concentric and the red surround becomes an even band all round. The driver then sinks back past rest (overshoot 0.50) and settles at 0.42, a visible pump of the dish.

accept.check: The three rings are concentric: the red surround is an even band all the way round.

changes.problem: Between 25 and 48 px the full land breaks into specks and slivers, and in one colour the 32 px figure is noise.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, 'black only' and 'white only' at 32 px: the land breaks into specks and slivers that merge with the dish's rings. SMALL is 24 px, so 32 px still carries all the land. The land-free 'small, black' cut at 32 px is clean, but it is no longer a globe.
changes.description: From 25 to 48 px, draw the figure with only the land pieces of at least 0.06 of the disc's area, which keeps North and South America. Drop the crescent beyond the dish and every island. The dish, the knock-outs and the clearances stay the same. The land-free cut stays at 24 px and under.
changes.expected: At 32 and 48 px the figure reads as a globe: two continents and the driver, clean in colour and in one colour. The Earth survives down to the favicon size where the land-free cut takes over.

accept.at: sheet 2, black only and white only, 32 px
accept.check: Each 32 px figure shows the dish's ring and cap plus exactly two land shapes (North and South America), with no specks or slivers.

changes.problem: A 1.06 swell of the dust cap is too small to see, so the hot core never flares on the kick.
changes.evidence: Card: a scale of 1.06 grows the cap by less than 0.01 of the radius, under 1 px at storyboard scale. No frame on sheet 3 shows the core change.
changes.expected: On each beat the yellow core flares from 0.40 to 0.48 of the dish's radius, and the orange band narrows from 0.30 to 0.22. Both return with the overshoot.

accept.check: The yellow dust cap is clearly larger than in frame 01, and the orange cone around it is a visibly narrower band.

changes.problem: Everything the push moves sits inside the dish, among three warm colours of similar brightness. The red rim, the dish's only strong edge, never moves, so the kick has no punch at a glance.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3 trace at 0.00-0.03 s: 0.06 %. The dish is about 2 % of the frame. In my rebuild of the frames, even depth 0.0 with a 1.20 cap lifts that frame only to about 0.08 %.
changes.description: On the push, scale the whole driver (surround, cone and cap together) 1.05 times about the dish's centre. It follows the same timing as the depth: out by 0.06 s, held to 0.13 s, back through the overshoot, and at rest by 0.42 s. The globe and the land do not move.
changes.expected: The dish visibly throws forward on the beat, its red rim stepping out about 0.02 of the radius toward the edge, then settles. The kick reads at a glance and at small sizes, while the cabinet (the globe) stays still, as a real speaker's does.

changes.problem: The 18-degree lean drops the dish to about half past two. There it reads as a speaker on the side of a ball rather than the Death Star's upper-right divot, and it tips North America off its axis.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 #1 and sheet 2 at 300 px: the dish's centre sits about 24 degrees above the horizontal through the globe's centre, and its lower rim dips 0.19 of the radius below the midline. North America leans to the right.
changes.expected: The whole figure turns 10 degrees counter-clockwise. The dish's centre sits at about half past one to two o'clock (about 39 degrees with the new DISH.at), where the Death Star's dish sits. The Americas stand upright and read faster as Earth.

accept.check: The dish's centre sits between half past one and two o'clock from the globe's centre, and North America stands upright rather than leaning right.

changes.problem: The ring drags out through a long faint tail that blurs the end of each beat.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3 frame 05 (0.53 s): a ghost of the ring, barely visible. Trace 0.43-0.53 s: falling from 0.0006 to 0.0002. Nobody reads this motion, but it delays the clean rest.
changes.expected: The ring crosses the globe faster and is gone by 0.45 s. Each beat reads as kick, ripple, rest, with a clean still of about half a second before the next.

accept.check: No trace of the ring is visible.

most_important: Move the dish in to DISH.at (0.32, 0.34). The owner asked for more earth on the outside. Today, at 300 px, only about 25 px of globe and a hairline of land separate the dish from the edge. This move turns that into a real crescent of Europe and West Africa without touching the divot's 24-degree size.
out_of_scope: The fixed palette. The red surround has the same luminance as the green land (1.02:1) and only 1.4:1 against the blue ocean, so the dish's outer edge depends on hue alone. In greyscale, for red-green colour-blind viewers and at 16-32 px, it melts into the land and sea. Colour cannot fix this without changing the palette; the one-colour figures are the remedy.

The dish as a red, orange and yellow driver. On a blue-green globe, three warm concentric rings read first as a target or a heat-map hotspot (a 'burning Earth') before a speaker. This is fixed, but it is the first reading a stranger is likely to make, which is why the motion has to do the work of saying 'speaker'.
for_owner: Divot size. At 24 degrees the dish is 48 degrees of arc across, as wide as the North Atlantic between Newfoundland and Iberia, so the coasts on both sides get trimmed wherever it sits. At 21-22 degrees, still larger than the Death Star's, Newfoundland, Iberia and West Africa survive and the earth wraps around the dish. You have said a slightly larger divot is fine, so this trade is your call.

Violet. My advice is to leave the trench off, because it reads as a sash or an orbit and splits the globe. I would also drop the violet cap, because it turns the driver into a pupil. Both add a sixth colour and more detail, against 'minimal and polished'. Keep one only if tying this figure to the six-colour main mark matters more to you.
The lean. If 18 degrees deliberately echoes the main mark's tilt, keep it and skip change 8.

The tone of the ring. As a knock-out it briefly cuts through the globe's outline, and on ink it is a dark band through the Earth, which some will read as the Death Star doing its job. Confirm that this tone is wanted.

The Death Star itself. The land-free small cut, in black above all, is effectively the Death Star icon. Clear the reference with counsel before it goes on products for a decade, and keep land at every size above 24 px (change 5) so the figure stays a globe.
